data.narrative:
AnySignal is a Series A-stage company in Space & Aerospace that has raised $34M+ to date. The sector comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though no near-peer private company set at identical stage and valuation tier exists.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: Stage-Progression anchoring. Using the $34M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation at entry, a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier to the next funding round yields $68M. This represents the median implied valuation. Public-Comp anchoring cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue; while the Space & Aerospace sector trades at a 23.9x P/S median across six tickers, AnySignal's revenue is not on file. Peer-Median triangulation is not viable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and tier yields fewer than three datapoints.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $58M to $78M, centered on $68M, reflecting ±15% variance around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include absence of revenue disclosure (limiting multiple-based methods), limited visibility into comparable Series A Space & Aerospace exits, and typical private-stage information asymmetry. A two-method or revenue-informed triangulation would strengthen conviction materially.
